title: Flat base change of the conormal algebra of a closed immersion
statement:
Let $g:X\to X'$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I'$, and let $(Z,i,f)$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $g$ and $i'$, so that $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ and $f:Z\to Z'$ satisfies $g\circ i=i'\circ f$. Let $\mathcal G'=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal G'_n$ and $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal G_n$ be the conormal algebras of $i'$ and $i$ [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], and let $f^*\mathcal G'$ be the pulled-back quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra [def-pc-module-pullback]. There is a unique morphism of graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebras
$$c:f^*\mathcal G'\longrightarrow\mathcal G$$
such that for every pair of affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq X'$ with $g(U)\subseteq U'$, writing $I'=\mathcal I'(U')$ and $I=\mathcal I(U)=I'R$, the map $c$ on sections over $i^{-1}U$ is, under the identifications of [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], the map
$$\bigoplus_{n\geq0}(I'^n/I'^{n+1})\otimes_{R'}R\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n/I^{n+1},\qquad [a]\otimes r\longmapsto[g^\sharp(a)\,r].$$
In degree $0$ it is the identity of $\mathcal O_Z=f^*\mathcal O_{Z'}$, and in degree $1$ it is the canonical conormal map $f^*\mathcal C_{Z'/X'}\to\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The map $c$ is surjective. If $g$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], then $c$ is an isomorphism of graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebras.

source.place: Divisors, Lemma 0635 (divisors-lemma-conormal-algebra-functorial-flat), with the map of Lemma 0634 (divisors-lemma-conormal-algebra-functorial), case of closed immersions

proof.text: Compatible affine charts cover. For $x\in X$ and any neighbourhood $H$ of $x$, choose an affine $U'\subseteq X'$ containing $g(x)$ and then an affine $U\subseteq H\cap g^{-1}U'$ containing $x$. Since $i$ is a closed immersion, its inverse images $W=i^{-1}U$ form an affine basis of $Z$, with $W=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ and $W'=i'^{-1}U'=\operatorname{Spec}(R'/I')$ by [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. The Cartesian hypothesis and [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image] identify $\mathcal I$ with the image of $g^*\mathcal I'\to\mathcal O_X$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] therefore gives $I=I'R$ on these charts. No affineness of intersections or Noetherian hypothesis is used.

source.place: 0634–0635: compatible affine neighbourhoods and the ideal of a Cartesian closed immersion; Schemes 01JU

proof.text: Fix a compatible pair and write $A=R'$, $B=R$, $J=I'$, $K=I=JB$, and $\phi=g^\sharp:A\to B$. The graded pieces on $W'$ and $W$ are the modules $M_n=J^n/J^{n+1}$ and $N_n=K^n/K^{n+1}$ by [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to $f|_W:W\to W'$: the source degree-$n$ sections are $M_n\otimes_{A/J}(B/K)$. They are canonically $M_n\otimes_A B$: the map $m\otimes b\mapsto m\otimes\bar b$ has inverse $m\otimes\bar b\mapsto m\otimes b$. A change of lift by $\sum\phi(j_l)b_l\in K$ gives $\sum j_lm\otimes b_l=0$, since $JM_n=0$; tensor balancing verifies the two inverses. This fixes the source identification and its normalization on pulled-back sections.

source.place: 0634: affine formula for the pulled-back graded pieces; Schemes 01I9

proof.text: Define $c_n$ on each such chart by $[a]\otimes b\mapsto[\phi(a)b]$. The identity $K^n=J^nB$ follows by expanding products of generators of $K=JB$; conversely $\phi(a_1\cdots a_n)b$ is a product of $n$ elements of $K$ times $b$. For $n=0$ both ideals are the whole ring. Thus the formula lands in $N_n$. Changing $a$ by $u\in J^{n+1}$ changes its value by $\phi(u)b\in K^{n+1}$, and $\phi(ra)b=\phi(a)\phi(r)b$ proves balancing over $A$. Additivity in $a,b$ gives a well-defined $B/K$-linear map on the tensor quotient. These verifications are direct computations with ideals and tensor products.

source.place: 0634–0635: explicit affine map and its well-definedness

proof.text: Convert each linear map in step 3 into a morphism of quasi-coherent sheaves on $W$ by the affine tilde adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], using the quasi-coherence and identifications of step 2. These local sheaf maps agree on overlaps. Here is the restriction check: on a principal target refinement, a quotient section has the form $[a]/s^r$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. On a source refinement where $\phi(s)$ is invertible, its pullback times $b$ is sent by either recipe to $[\phi(a)b]/\phi(s)^r$. Source restriction applies the ring restriction to $b$ and to $\phi(a)$, which commutes with $g^\sharp$ and with taking quotient classes. Principal opens form a basis on each affine target. For two target charts, refine their intersection by affine opens, and within each original chart by principal opens; refine their inverse images by affine source opens. On these refinements the displayed fraction calculation proves equality on the pulled-back local generators, which generate the tensor pullback by [def-pc-module-pullback]. It proves equality of the two sheaf maps on an open cover of each overlap, without assuming the overlap affine. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] in each degree to obtain $c_n:f^*\mathcal G'_n\to\mathcal G_n$. The same argument shows that it satisfies step 3 on every compatible affine pair, not only a selected cover.

source.place: 0634: construction from the affine formula, expanding its omitted restriction and gluing check

proof.text: The maps $c_n$ preserve multiplication and unit. On local tensor representatives, using the multiplication specified in [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], both $c_{m+n}(([a]\otimes b)([a']\otimes b'))$ and $c_m([a]\otimes b)c_n([a']\otimes b')$ equal $[\phi(aa')bb']$. The degree-zero unit goes to $[1]$. Bilinearity extends these equalities to sums of pure tensors; they then hold as sheaf identities since pure tensors locally generate the tensor sheaf [def-pc-module-pullback]. The definition [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] extends the homogeneous maps to the direct-sum sheaves and gives a graded algebra morphism $c$. Pullback commutes with this direct sum because it is a left adjoint [def-pc-module-pullback]: maps from the pullback of the sum to any module are, by adjunction and the coproduct property, families of maps from the pullbacks of its summands. This identifies its homogeneous pieces with those used above. Finally, two graded morphisms satisfying the required affine formula agree degreewise on this cover, so the uniqueness in [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] proves uniqueness of $c$.

source.place: 0634: graded algebra laws and characterization by affine formula

proof.text: In degree zero the formula is $(A/J)\otimes_A B\to B/K$, $[a]\otimes b\mapsto[\phi(a)b]$. Under the isomorphism $f^*\mathcal O_{Z'}\simeq\mathcal O_Z$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] this is the identity: $1\otimes\bar b$ maps to $\bar b$. In degree one, [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra] identifies the pieces with the conormal sheaves, and the characterization in [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-functorial] gives the same formula on every $[a]\otimes b$. Local generation and uniqueness from step 4 therefore identify $c_1$ with that canonical conormal map.

source.place: 0634 and 0630–0633: degree-zero and degree-one normalizations; Morphisms 01R4

proof.text: Each $c_n$ is surjective on sections over every compatible affine $W$. Indeed, since $K^n=J^nB$, write a representative of a class in $N_n$ as $\sum_l\phi(a_l)b_l$ with $a_l\in J^n$; its preimage is $\sum_l[a_l]\otimes b_l$. This includes $n=0$. For an arbitrary section of $\mathcal G$ near a point, the direct-sum sheaf convention [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] expresses it locally as a finite sum of homogeneous sections. Refine further to a compatible affine $W$ and lift those finitely many homogeneous sections by the preceding formula. Thus every section locally lifts, proving that $c$ is surjective as a sheaf morphism (equivalently on all stalks by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks]). This does not assert surjectivity on sections over every non-affine open.

source.place: 0635: surjectivity, with the affine ideal-generator argument and sheaf locality

proof.text: Now suppose $g$ is flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], $B$ is flat as an $A$-module on every compatible affine pair. For each $n$, the inclusion $j_n:J^n/J^{n+1}\hookrightarrow A/J^{n+1}$ is injective: its kernel consists of classes represented by elements of $J^{n+1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to this injection; hence $j_n\otimes_A B$ is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] to the ideal $J^{n+1}$ and use $J^{n+1}B=K^{n+1}$ from step 3 to identify its target with $B/K^{n+1}$. The resulting injective map sends $[a]\otimes b$ to $[\phi(a)b]\in B/K^{n+1}$. It factors as $c_n$ followed by the inclusion $K^n/K^{n+1}\hookrightarrow B/K^{n+1}$. Therefore $c_n$ is injective. Combined with step 7 it is bijective for every $n$, including $n=0$. This proves the all-degrees assertion using flatness, not by extrapolating the degree-one conormal theorem.

source.place: 0635: flat affine calculation; Algebra 00HD and tensor-quotient comparison

proof.text: By the affine tilde equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], the bijective chart maps of step 8 induce isomorphisms on each $W$. Their inverses agree on overlaps: both invert the same restricted $c_n$, and the inverse of a fixed map is unique. The gluing theorem [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] gives a global inverse for every $c_n$. Extend these inverses to the graded direct sums using [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. They respect multiplication and unit because applying the injective $c$ reduces each required equality to the multiplication and unit equalities of step 5. Hence the inverse is a graded algebra morphism, proving that $c$ is an isomorphism of graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebras.
